children: MTU Aero Engines' profit margins and cash flow will perform much better than expected, Bernstein analysts write. Margins will likely reach 30% by 2030 as older engines stay in service longer, newer engines becoming more reliable, and the reduced need for spare parts keep profits high, Bernstein says. Moreover, as investment spending levels out, airline compensation payments end, and unpaid bills are collected, cash generation will rebound to nearly 100% of profits by 2030, analysts say. The aircraft groundings stemming from issues with the Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan engines are improving for the first time since 2023, giving management better operational visibility and credibility to provide precise long-term guidance, Bernstein says. Shares are up 1.1% at 361.90 euros. (anthony.orunagoriainoff@dowjones.com)
